errors.name: UnexpectedCharacter
errors.meaning: A character that cannot begin any token.

errors.name: UnterminatedString
errors.meaning: A string literal that is never closed.

errors.name: InvalidNumberLiteral
errors.meaning: A malformed number literal: a letter touching it, an exponent without digits, or a value too large.
errors.detail: **`E1-003`** is raised for a number literal that is too large to represent (`1e400`, or one written with hundreds of digits), and for a number that a letter touches: an exponent without digits (`1e`), a hexadecimal form (`0x10`), digit separators (`1_000`), or a word written against a number (`2x`).

errors.name: InconsistentIndentation
errors.meaning: Indentation that does not line up with the enclosing block.

errors.name: ColonSpaceBeforeNotAllowed
errors.meaning: A space before the colon that opens a block.

errors.name: UnterminatedComment
errors.meaning: A block comment that is never closed.

errors.name: UnexpectedToken
errors.meaning: The token found cannot appear here. Every syntax problem found while tokenizing or parsing is reported with this code.
errors.detail: The program is not valid CuffScript. The message says what was expected and the caret shows where the parser gave up. The usual causes are a declaration or an assignment that is not written `TYPE NAME = value` or `NAME = value` (the old `set`, `change` and `to` forms get a hint that says what to write), a block with no `end`, a body that is not indented, a missing `do:`, a space before a colon, a string with no closing quote and a stray character. Put the first error right and run again: later errors are often caused by the first.
errors.report:
[E2-001] Syntax Error at line 1, column 8
  |
1 | number x
  |        ^ expected the end of the line after the statement (got 'x')

  hint: to declare 'x' write `number x = value`

errors.name: ExpectedToken
errors.meaning: A specific token was required.

errors.name: MalformedFunctionDecl
errors.meaning: A malformed function declaration.

errors.name: MalformedControlFlow
errors.meaning: A malformed `if` or loop.

errors.name: MalformedImport
errors.meaning: A malformed `use` statement.

errors.name: UnbalancedBlock
errors.meaning: A block opened without a matching `end`.

errors.name: InvalidAssignmentTarget
errors.meaning: Something that cannot be assigned to.

errors.name: NestingTooDeep
errors.meaning: Code nested deeper than the nesting limit, or a single expression longer than the expression limit.
errors.detail: **`E2-008`** is raised for code nested deeper than the nesting limit, or a single expression longer than the expression limit, and **`E2-009`** for a program or shell entry larger than the source size limit. **`E3-011`** is the same kind of error for a pattern: one that is too large or nested too deeply. The values are in [limits](limits.md).

errors.name: SourceTooLarge
errors.meaning: A program or shell entry larger than the source size limit.
errors.detail: **`E2-008`** is raised for code nested deeper than the nesting limit, or a single expression longer than the expression limit, and **`E2-009`** for a program or shell entry larger than the source size limit. **`E3-011`** is the same kind of error for a pattern: one that is too large or nested too deeply. The values are in [limits](limits.md).

errors.name: DuplicateDeclaration
errors.meaning: A name declared again where the same function or program already declares it.
errors.detail: A name is declared a second time where the same function, or the top level of the program, already declares it: in the same block, in a block inside it, or as a parameter or a loop variable with the name of a variable declared before. Give the second one another name, or assign to the first (`total = 2`). Two blocks side by side may declare the same name, and so may two functions. It is also raised for a second function of the same name at the top level of one file: both cannot be meant, so rename one or remove it (a later shell entry may still declare a function again).
errors.report:
[E2-010] Syntax Error at line 2, column 8
  |
2 | number total = 2
  |        ^^^^^ 'total' is already declared here

  hint: give it a new value with `total = ...`, or choose another name

errors.name: RegexUnclosedGroup
errors.meaning: A `(` or named capture that is never closed, or a `<` that does not begin a `<name:...>` capture.
errors.detail: A pattern has a `(` that is never closed, or a `<` that does not start a named capture such as `<year:[num]4>`. Close the group, or escape the character you meant literally: `\(` or `\<`.
errors.report:
[E3-001] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"(a")
  |                   ^^^^^ in pattern "(a": unclosed '(' — missing ')'

errors.name: RegexUnclosedBracket
errors.meaning: A `[` that is never closed.
errors.detail: A pattern has a `[` that is never closed. Close it, or write `\[` to match a bracket.
errors.report:
[E3-002] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"[num")
  |                   ^^^^^^^ in pattern "[num": unclosed '[' — missing ']'

errors.name: RegexInvalidColonSpacing
errors.meaning: Wrong spacing around the colon of a token such as `[one:a|b]`.
errors.detail: There is a space between a token's word and its colon. Write `[one:a|b]`, with the colon right after the word.
errors.report:
[E3-003] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"[one :a|b]")
  |                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ in pattern "[one :a|b]": no space is allowed before ':' in '[one:...]'

  hint: write [one:...] instead of [one :...]

errors.name: RegexInvalidQuantifierRange
errors.meaning: A repeat range or character range that cannot match anything, such as `5~2` or `[z-a]`, or a repeat count above the repeat limit.
errors.detail: A repeat range must run from the smaller number to the larger. `5~2` cannot match anything. The same code is raised for a character range written backwards, such as `[z-a]`, and for a repeat count larger than the pattern repeat limit (see [limits](limits.md)).
errors.report:
[E3-004] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"[num]5~2")
  |                   ^^^^^^^^^^^ in pattern "[num]5~2": quantifier range 5~2 has a start greater than its end

errors.name: RegexStackedQuantifier
errors.meaning: Two quantifiers applied to the same item, such as `[num]++`.
errors.detail: A pattern item can have one quantifier. `[num]++` has two. Keep one of them.
errors.report:
[E3-005] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"[num]++")
  |                   ^^^^^^^^^^ in pattern "[num]++": quantifiers cannot be stacked directly on top of each other

  hint: combine into a single quantifier, e.g. use '+' or a 'N~M' range, not both

errors.name: RegexEmptyToken
errors.meaning: An empty token or an empty alternative.
errors.detail: A token with nothing in it, or an alternative with nothing between its bars. `[one:]` and `[one:a||b]` are both errors.
errors.report:
[E3-006] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"[one:]")
  |                   ^^^^^^^^^ in pattern "[one:]": '[one:...]' has no alternatives

errors.name: RegexUnknownToken
errors.meaning: A bracket token whose name before the colon is not `one`. A pattern cannot reach it today: an unknown word in brackets is read as a set of characters.

errors.name: RegexInvalidEscape
errors.meaning: A backslash that escapes nothing, or something that cannot be escaped.
errors.detail: A backslash must be followed by one of the characters it can escape: `[ ] ( ) { } < > + * ? ~ | . \ : !`. Pattern escapes such as `\d` do not exist; use `[num]`. A backslash at the very end of a pattern is also this error.
errors.report:
[E3-008] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"\d")
  |                   ^^^^^ in pattern "\d": '\d' is not a recognized escape sequence

  hint: CuffScript patterns only support escaping literal symbols such as \. \+ \( \[ — there is no \d/\w/\s style escape

errors.name: RegexDanglingQuantifier
errors.meaning: A `~` that is neither part of a repeat range nor escaped, such as `a~b`.
errors.detail: A `~` that is not part of a repeat range. To match a tilde, write `\~`.
errors.report:
[E3-009] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"a~b")
  |                   ^^^^^^ in pattern "a~b": '~' must be followed by a number (as in '~5') or preceded by one (as in '3~5', '3~')

  hint: use \~ to match a literal '~'

errors.name: RegexUnexpectedCharacter
errors.meaning: A character that cannot appear at this point of a pattern.
errors.detail: A closing `)`, `]` or `>` with nothing to close. Escape it (`\)`) to match the character itself.
errors.report:
[E3-010] Regex Syntax Error at line 1, column 19
  |
1 | print("x" matches p"a)")
  |                   ^^^^^ in pattern "a)": unexpected ')' with no matching opener

errors.name: RegexPatternTooComplex
errors.meaning: A pattern larger than the pattern size limit, or nested deeper than the pattern nesting limit.
errors.detail: **`E2-008`** is raised for code nested deeper than the nesting limit, or a single expression longer than the expression limit, and **`E2-009`** for a program or shell entry larger than the source size limit. **`E3-011`** is the same kind of error for a pattern: one that is too large or nested too deeply. The values are in [limits](limits.md).

errors.name: RegexStepLimitExceeded
errors.meaning: Matching used more steps than its budget allows.
errors.detail: A pattern ran past the budget of matching steps. Patterns that nest a repeat inside a repeat, like `([any]*)*`, can take an enormous number of steps on a text that almost matches. Simplify the pattern. This one can be caught with `or_else`; `E3-102` (time) and `E3-103` (recursion depth) are the same kind of error and are handled the same way.
errors.report:
[E3-101] Regex Runtime Error at line 2, column 9
  |
2 | print(s matches p"([any]*)*x")
  |         ^^^^^^^ pattern matching exceeded the maximum step limit (possible catastrophic backtracking)

  hint: simplify the pattern — avoid nested unbounded quantifiers like ([any]+)+

errors.name: RegexTimeout
errors.meaning: Matching ran longer than its time budget allows.

errors.name: RegexRecursionLimitExceeded
errors.meaning: Matching recursed deeper than its limit.

errors.name: UndefinedVariable
errors.meaning: A variable that has not been declared, or is not visible here.
errors.detail: A name that was never declared, was declared later in the program, or lives in another scope. Check the spelling. Inside a function, a variable of the main program is only visible after `global name`.
errors.report:
[E4-001] Runtime Error at line 1, column 7
  |
1 | print(missing)
  |       ^^^^^^^ undefined variable 'missing'

errors.name: UndefinedFunction
errors.meaning: A function that has not been declared.
errors.detail: A function that does not exist. Check the spelling, and remember that library functions need their `use DLC:...` line first; `length` needs one of the string, list or map libraries.
errors.report:
[E4-002] Runtime Error at line 1, column 7
  |
1 | print(missing_fn(1))
  |       ^^^^^^^^^^ undefined function 'missing_fn'

  hint: check the spelling, or make sure it's declared before this point

errors.name: ConstantReassignment
errors.meaning: A constant that is changed after it was created.
errors.detail: A constant, or a constant list, was changed. Declare the value without `constant` if it has to change. To change a constant list, copy it first into an ordinary list.
errors.report:
[E4-003] Runtime Error at line 2, column 1
  |
2 | MAX = 2
  | ^^^ cannot change constant 'MAX'

errors.name: InvalidConstantName
errors.meaning: A constant whose name is not all uppercase letters, digits and underscores.
errors.detail: A constant's name must be all capital letters, digits and underscores, so that a constant stands out from a variable: `MAX_USERS`.
errors.report:
[E4-004] Runtime Error at line 1, column 17
  |
1 | constant number max = 1
  |                 ^^^ constant name 'max' must be written in ALL CAPS (uppercase letters, digits, underscores only)

  hint: for example: MAX

errors.name: TypeMismatch
errors.meaning: A value of the wrong type for an operation.
errors.detail: An operation was given the wrong kind of value, such as `"a" + 1`, a comparison between a number and a string, or a library function given a list where it wants a string. Convert explicitly with `to_str` or `to_number`.
errors.report:
[E4-005] Runtime Error at line 1, column 11
  |
1 | print("a" + 1)
  |           ^ cannot add str and number

  hint: '+' works on number+number, str+str, or list+list

errors.name: DivisionByZero
errors.meaning: Division or remainder by zero, or zero to a negative power.
errors.detail: A division or remainder by zero, or zero raised to a negative power. Test the divisor before dividing.
errors.report:
[E4-006] Runtime Error at line 1, column 9
  |
1 | print(1 / 0)
  |         ^ division by zero

errors.name: ZeroIndexAccess
errors.meaning: Position 0, which does not exist (positions start at 1).
errors.detail: Positions start at 1. Position `0` does not exist; the first element is `1` and the last is `-1`.
errors.report:
[E4-007] Runtime Error at line 1, column 12
  |
1 | print("abc"[0])
  |            ^ index 0 does not exist — CuffScript indexing starts at 1

  hint: use 1 for the first element, or -1 for the last

errors.name: IndexOutOfRange
errors.meaning: A position outside a list, string or slice.
errors.detail: A position past the end of a list or string, or a slice that runs past it. Positions run from `1` to the length, and from `-1` (the last) backwards.
errors.report:
[E4-008] Runtime Error at line 1, column 12
  |
1 | print("abc"[5])
  |            ^ index 5 is out of range (length 3)

errors.name: KeyNotFound
errors.meaning: A map key that is not present.
errors.detail: A map has no such key. Ask `map_has_key(m, key)` first, or recover with `or_else`.
errors.report:
[E4-009] Runtime Error at line 2, column 8
  |
2 | print(m["b"])
  |        ^ key "b" does not exist in this map

errors.name: ArgumentCountMismatch
errors.meaning: A call with the wrong number of arguments.
errors.detail: A function was called with too many or too few arguments. Compare the call with the function's parameters, or with its entry in the [function index](functions.md).
errors.report:
[E4-010] Runtime Error at line 1, column 7
  |
1 | print(type_of(1, 2))
  |       ^^^^^^^ type_of() expects 1 argument(s), got 2

errors.name: NotCallable
errors.meaning: Calling something that is not a function.

errors.name: InvalidOperand
errors.meaning: An operand an operator cannot work with.

errors.name: LocalVariableOutOfScope
errors.meaning: A local variable used outside the function that declared it.

errors.name: InvalidCollectionOperation
errors.meaning: An operation a list or map does not support.

errors.name: ElementNotFound
errors.meaning: A value to remove that is not in the list.
errors.detail: `remove` was given a value that is not in the list. Check with `contains` first, or remove by position with `remove at`.
errors.report:
[E4-015] Runtime Error at line 2, column 1
  |
2 | remove "x" from a
  | ^^^^^^ value not found in list — nothing to remove

errors.name: UnsupportedOperation
errors.meaning: An operation not supported here, such as `return value` outside a function.
errors.detail: A `return` with a value at the top level of a program, outside any function. Put the code in a function, or show the value with `print`.
errors.report:
[E4-016] Runtime Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | return 1
  | ^^^^^^ 'return' with a value can only be used inside a function

  hint: at the top level, show a value with print(...)

errors.name: StackOverflow
errors.meaning: More calls active at once than the call depth limit allows, or nesting inside the engine deeper than the native stack budget allows.
errors.detail: Recursion went too deep: more calls were active at once than the call depth limit allows. Make sure the recursion has a base case that is always reached. The same error ends nesting inside the engine that reaches the stack budget, such as a field whose default value makes another object of the same class (see [limits](limits.md)).
errors.example:
func f() do:
    f()
end
f()
errors.report:
[E4-017] Runtime Error at line 2, column 5
  |
2 |     f()
  |     ^ maximum call depth (1000) exceeded while calling 'f' — check for infinite recursion

  in f, called from:
    line 2 in f: f() (999 times)
    line 4: f()

errors.name: NestedFunctionNotSupported
errors.meaning: A function declared inside another function.
errors.detail: A function was declared inside another function. Declare every function at the top level; functions are visible everywhere.
errors.report:
[E4-018] Runtime Error at line 2, column 5
  |
2 |     func inner() do:
  |     ^^^^ nested function definitions are not supported ('inner' is defined inside another function)

  in outer, called from:
    line 5: outer()

  hint: move 'inner' to the top level

errors.name: AwaitOnNonAsync
errors.meaning: `await` applied to a function that is not `async`, or to a value that is not a task.
errors.detail: `await` was applied to a call of a function that is not `async`, or to a value that is not a `Task`. Declare the function `async func`, or drop the `await`; to wait for a task, `await` the `Task` value its call gave.
errors.report:
[E4-019] Runtime Error at line 3, column 1
  |
3 | await f()
  | ^^^^^ 'await' can only be used with an async function; 'f' is not declared async

  hint: declare it with 'async func f(...) do:', or call it without 'await'

errors.name: DeclarationTypeMismatch
errors.meaning: A declared type that does not match the value.
errors.detail: A value does not have the type the variable, field, loop variable or `or_else` name was declared with: `number n = "x"`, or `n = "x"` after `number n = 1`. Store a value of the declared type, or declare the type the value really has; a variable that holds different types is declared `any`, and so is one that may hold the `empty` of a failed `find` or `match`, because `empty` is not a `str` or a `match`.
errors.report:
[E4-020] Runtime Error at line 1, column 8
  |
1 | number n = "x"
  |        ^ cannot assign a str value to number variable 'n'

  hint: a variable keeps the type it was declared with (number); use 'any' for a variable that holds different types

errors.name: InvalidGlobalDeclaration
errors.meaning: `global` outside a function body.
errors.detail: `global name` is only meaningful inside a function, where it makes a global variable visible. At the top level every variable is already in reach.
errors.report:
[E4-021] Runtime Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | global x
  | ^^^^^^ 'global' can only be used inside a function body

  hint: at the top level, every variable is already global

errors.name: ReturnOutsideFunction
errors.meaning: `return` outside any function.
errors.detail: A bare `return` outside any function. (With a value, it is `E4-016`.)
errors.report:
[E4-022] Runtime Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | return
  | ^^^^^^ 'return' cannot be used outside of a function

errors.name: StopOutsideLoop
errors.meaning: `stop` or `skip` outside any loop.
errors.detail: `stop` ends the nearest loop and `skip` goes on with its next pass. Both are errors anywhere else, including inside a function that is called from a loop.
errors.report:
[E4-023] Runtime Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | stop
  | ^^^^ 'stop' cannot be used outside of a loop

errors.name: FractionalIndex
errors.meaning: A position or range bound that is not a whole number.
errors.detail: A position or a range bound that is not a whole number. Round it first with `math_floor` or `math_round`.
errors.report:
[E4-024] Runtime Error at line 1, column 12
  |
1 | print("abc"[1.5])
  |            ^ str index must be a whole number, got 1.5

  hint: round it explicitly first (DLC:math's round/floor/ceil)

errors.name: InvalidArgumentValue
errors.meaning: An argument of the right type but a value the function or operator does not accept.
errors.detail: The argument has the right type, but a value the function cannot use: text that is not a number, a negative square root, an empty list where the function needs one element, and so on. The message says which. Check the value first, or recover with `or_else`.
errors.report:
[E4-025] Runtime Error at line 1, column 7
  |
1 | print(to_number("abc"))
  |       ^^^^^^^^^ to_number() could not parse "abc" as a number

errors.name: SizeLimitExceeded
errors.meaning: A string, list, map, class declaration, or number of tasks larger than its limit.
errors.detail: A string, list, map or class declaration grew past its limit, or too many tasks were started or are waiting at once (see [limits](limits.md)).
errors.report:
[E4-026] Runtime Error at line 2, column 7
  |
2 | print(str_repeat("abcdefgh", 1000000000))
  |       ^^^^^^^^^^ string exceeds the maximum allowed size

errors.name: PureFunctionGlobalAccess
errors.meaning: A `pure` function that reaches a global variable.
errors.detail: A `pure` function used a global variable. A pure function can use only its parameters and its own variables.
errors.example:
number g = 1
pure func f() do:
    global g
    return g
end
print(f())
errors.report:
[E4-027] Runtime Error at line 3, column 12
  |
3 |     global g
  |            ^ cannot access global variable 'g' from inside a pure function

  in f, called from:
    line 6: print(f())

  hint: remove the 'pure' keyword to allow this

errors.name: NetworkRequestFailed
errors.meaning: A network request that failed, timed out, or targeted a blocked address.
errors.detail: A network request could not be completed: the address is blocked or uses a scheme the library does not support, the server could not be reached, it took too long, or the answer was too large. The message says which. The example uses a scheme that is not supported, so it fails before any connection is made. The documentation checks run with the network switched off, so they do not run this example.

errors.name: PureFunctionImpureCall
errors.meaning: A `pure` function that calls a function that is not `pure`.
errors.detail: A `pure` function called a function of the program that is not `pure`. Mark the called function `pure` too, or do not use `pure` here. Library functions may be called freely.
errors.example:
func helper() do:
end
pure func f() do:
    helper()
end
f()
errors.report:
[E4-029] Runtime Error at line 4, column 5
  |
4 |     helper()
  |     ^^^^^^ a pure function cannot call non-pure function 'helper'

  in f, called from:
    line 6: f()

  hint: mark 'helper' as pure, or remove 'pure' from the caller

errors.name: ParameterTypeMismatch
errors.meaning: An argument that does not match the parameter's declared type.
errors.detail: An argument does not match the type declared for the parameter (`number a`). Convert it before the call, or declare the parameter `any`.
errors.report:
[E4-030] Runtime Error at line 3, column 1
  |
3 | f("x")
  | ^ f(): parameter 'a' expects number, got str

  hint: declared as 'number a' in the parameter list

errors.name: UnknownClass
errors.meaning: A class name that is not declared, used as a type, in `extends`, in `isa` or as a constructor.
errors.detail: A class name that is not declared: as a type, after `extends`, after `isa`, or in a `with` or a declaration. Check the spelling, and remember that a class belongs at the top level of a file or of a module that was loaded with `use`.
errors.report:
[E4-031] Runtime Error at line 1, column 9
  |
1 | print(1 isa Ghost)
  |         ^^^ unknown class 'Ghost'

  hint: declare it with `class Ghost do: ... end` at the top level of a file, and check the spelling

errors.name: InvalidInheritance
errors.meaning: A class that inherits from itself, through its ancestors, from something that is not a class, or from `Task`.
errors.detail: A class that extends itself, directly or through its ancestors, extends something that is not a class, or extends the built-in `Task`.
errors.example:
class A extends A do:
end
errors.report:
[E4-032] Runtime Error at line 1, column 17
  |
1 | class A extends A do:
  |                 ^ class 'A' cannot extend itself

errors.name: UnknownMember
errors.meaning: A field or method that the object's class does not have.
errors.detail: The class has no such field or method. The report lists the fields the class has; the usual cause is a misspelt name.
errors.example:
class Dog do:
    str name = "Rex"
end
Dog d = Dog()
print(d.nmae)
errors.report:
[E4-033] Runtime Error at line 5, column 9
  |
5 | print(d.nmae)
  |         ^^^^ class 'Dog' has no field 'nmae'

  hint: fields: name

errors.name: PrivateMemberAccess
errors.meaning: A `private` field or method used outside the class that declares it.
errors.detail: A `private` field or method was used outside the class that declares it. Child classes are outside too: only the methods of the declaring class can use it.
errors.example:
class Safe do:
    private number code = 1234
end
print(Safe().code)
errors.report:
[E4-034] Runtime Error at line 4, column 14
  |
4 | print(Safe().code)
  |              ^^^^ 'code' is a private field of 'Safe'

  hint: it can only be used inside the methods of Safe itself

errors.name: NotAnObject
errors.meaning: A `.name` access or a `with` block applied to a value that is not an object.
errors.detail: A `.name` was used on a value that is not an object, or `with` was given one. Only objects have fields and methods.
errors.report:
[E4-035] Runtime Error at line 2, column 9
  |
2 | print(n.size)
  |         ^^^^ cannot read '.size' of a number value: it is not an object

  hint: only objects made from a class have fields and methods

errors.name: ClassNotTopLevel
errors.meaning: A class declared inside a block or a function; classes belong at the top level of a file.
errors.detail: A class was declared inside a block or a function. Move it to the top level of the file.
errors.report:
[E4-036] Runtime Error at line 2, column 5
  |
2 |     class Inner do:
  |     ^^^^^ a class can only be declared at the top level of a file

  hint: move the class out of the block or function that contains it

errors.name: DuplicateMember
errors.meaning: Two fields or methods of one class with the same name.
errors.detail: A class declares two members with the same name, or a child declares a field its parent already has, or a method has the name of a field. Rename one of them.
errors.example:
class Box do:
    number size = 1
    number size = 2
end
errors.report:
[E4-037] Runtime Error at line 3, column 5
  |
3 |     number size = 2
  |     ^^^^^^ 'size' is declared twice in class 'Box'

errors.name: ClassNameConflict
errors.meaning: A class named like a function, another class, or a built-in.
errors.detail: A class has the name of a function, of another class or of a built-in class (`Error`, `Task`). Classes and functions share one namespace.
errors.report:
[E4-038] Runtime Error at line 4, column 1
  |
4 | class Report do:
  | ^^^^^ class 'Report' has the same name as a function

  hint: classes and functions share one namespace; rename one of them

errors.name: InvalidClassName
errors.meaning: A class whose name does not start with an uppercase letter.
errors.detail: A class name must start with a capital letter, so that a class stands out from a variable.
errors.report:
[E4-039] Runtime Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | class point do:
  | ^^^^^ class name 'point' must start with an uppercase letter

  hint: for example: Point

errors.name: MethodNotCalled
errors.meaning: A method used as a value, or a field called as a method.
errors.detail: A method was used without the parentheses that call it, or a field was called like a method. Write `object.method(...)` for a method and `object.field` for a field.
errors.report:
[E4-040] Runtime Error at line 6, column 13
  |
6 | print(Dog().bark)
  |             ^^^^ 'bark' is a method of 'Dog', not a field

  hint: call it with parentheses: bark(...)

errors.name: PureFunctionFieldWrite
errors.meaning: A `pure` function or method that changes a field.
errors.detail: A `pure` function or method changed a field. A pure method may read fields but not write them; remove `pure`, or return the new value instead.
errors.example:
class Counter do:
    number n = 0

    pure func bump() do:
        self.n = self.n + 1
    end
end
Counter().bump()
errors.report:
[E4-041] Runtime Error at line 5, column 9
  |
5 |         self.n = self.n + 1
  |         ^^^^ a pure function cannot change a field

  in Counter.bump, called from:
    line 8: Counter().bump()

  hint: remove the 'pure' keyword to allow this

errors.name: HostFunctionFailed
errors.meaning: A function that the host program added reported a failure.
errors.detail: A function that the host program added with `Engine::addFunction` reported a failure (`Args::fail`, or a C++ exception it let out). The message is the host's own, after the function's name. A program can catch it with `or_else`; what the failure means is in the host's documentation. See [embedding](../guide/embedding.md).

errors.name: TaskDeadlock
errors.meaning: A task waits for something that can no longer happen: every task is waiting.
errors.detail: The program waits for something that can never happen: every task is waiting, and none waits for time to pass or for the network, so none can go on. Two tasks that await each other do this, and so does a task that awaits itself.
errors.example:
list tasks = []
async func wait_for(number which) do:
    global tasks
    return await tasks[which]
end
add wait_for(2) to tasks
add wait_for(1) to tasks
print(await tasks[1])
errors.report:
[E4-043] Runtime Error at line 8, column 7
  |
8 | print(await tasks[1])
  |       ^^^^^ this waits for something that cannot happen: every task is waiting

  hint: a task that waits for another, which waits for it in turn, never finishes

errors.name: HardwareUnsupported
errors.meaning: A part of the device that this device does not have, or that the host did not give (DLC:hardware).
errors.detail: A [`DLC:hardware`](dlc/hardware.md) function for a part that this device does not have, or that the host did not give the program: hardware is off unless the host gives it (`cuffc --hardware`, or `Engine::Options::hardware`). The message says which function, and the host's reason when it gave one (`hw_battery(): this computer has no battery`). Ask `hw_supports` first, or catch it with `or_else`.
errors.report:
[E4-044] Runtime Error at line 2, column 1
  |
2 | hw_led(0, true)
  | ^^^^^^ hw_led() is not supported on this device

  hint: ask hw_supports("led") first, or catch the error with or_else

errors.name: ModuleNotFound
errors.meaning: A module file that does not exist or cannot be read.
errors.detail: No such module file. `use nothing from ./lib` loads `./lib/nothing.cuff`, resolved against the folder of the script; check the folder and the file name.
errors.report:
[E5-001] Module Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | use nothing from ./lib
  | ^^^ could not find module file './lib/nothing.cuff' for 'use nothing from ./lib'

  hint: paths are resolved relative to the running script's directory

errors.name: ModuleParseFailed
errors.meaning: A module file that does not parse.
errors.detail: A module file was found but does not parse. The report shows the `use` line and then the module's own error, with its file and line.
errors.example:
use DLC:filesystem
file_write("broken.cuff", "number z = 1 +\n")
use broken from .
errors.report:
[E5-002] Module Error at line 3, column 1
  |
3 | use broken from .
  | ^^^ failed to parse module './broken.cuff': unexpected end of line in expression

  in './broken.cuff' [E2-001] at line 1, column 15:
    |
  1 | number z = 1 +
    |               ^ unexpected end of line in expression

errors.name: CircularImport
errors.meaning: Modules that import each other in a cycle.

errors.name: UnknownDLC
errors.meaning: A library name that does not exist.
errors.detail: There is no library by that name. The message lists the libraries that exist.
errors.report:
[E5-004] Module Error at line 1, column 5
  |
1 | use DLC:nothing
  |     ^^^ unknown DLC library 'DLC:nothing'

  hint: available libraries: DLC:math, DLC:string, DLC:time, DLC:datetime, DLC:random, DLC:list, DLC:map, DLC:convert, DLC:json, DLC:network, DLC:filesystem, DLC:csv, DLC:hash, DLC:path, DLC:hardware

errors.name: DLCFeatureUnavailable
errors.meaning: A call into a library that was switched off for this run (`--no-network`, `--no-filesystem`).
errors.detail: **`E5-005`** is raised by a call into `DLC:network` or `DLC:filesystem` when the host switched the library off (`--no-network`, `--no-filesystem`). The `use` line itself succeeds.

errors.name: ModuleAccessDenied
errors.meaning: A module path that is absolute, or resolves outside the allowed directory.
errors.detail: A module path that is absolute, or that leaves the allowed folder. See [the sandbox](../guide/modules.md#the-sandbox).
errors.report:
[E5-006] Module Error at line 1, column 1
  |
1 | use x from /etc
  | ^^^ absolute module paths are not allowed ('use x from /etc')

  hint: use a path relative to the running script, e.g. ./lib

errors.name: ModuleLimitExceeded
errors.meaning: Modules imported too deeply, or a module file larger than the source size limit.
errors.detail: **`E5-007`** is raised when modules load other modules too deeply, or when a module file is larger than the source size limit.

errors.name: FilesystemAccessDenied
errors.meaning: A file path that resolves outside the allowed directory.
errors.detail: A file path given to a `DLC:filesystem` function leaves the allowed folder or is absolute. Use a relative path below the script's folder.
errors.report:
[E5-008] Module Error at line 2, column 7
  |
2 | print(file_read("../x"))
  |       ^^^^^^^^^ DLC:filesystem's file_read("../x") reaches outside the sandboxed root

  hint: use a path relative to, and inside, the script's directory (or the host's configured rootDir)

errors.name: ExecutionStepLimit
errors.meaning: The run exceeded `--max-steps`.
errors.detail: **`E6-001`** and **`E6-002`** are raised when a run reaches `--max-steps` or `--timeout`; **`E6-003`** when the host runs out of memory. They end the program and cannot be caught: the budget is the host's decision, not the program's.

errors.name: ExecutionTimeout
errors.meaning: The run exceeded `--timeout`.
errors.detail: **`E6-001`** and **`E6-002`** are raised when a run reaches `--max-steps` or `--timeout`; **`E6-003`** when the host runs out of memory. They end the program and cannot be caught: the budget is the host's decision, not the program's.

errors.name: OutOfMemory
errors.meaning: The host ran out of memory.
errors.detail: **`E6-001`** and **`E6-002`** are raised when a run reaches `--max-steps` or `--timeout`; **`E6-003`** when the host runs out of memory. They end the program and cannot be caught: the budget is the host's decision, not the program's.

errors.name: ProgramError
errors.meaning: An error raised by the program itself with `fail`.
errors.detail: The program raised an error with `fail`, and nothing caught it. The message is the program's own. An error object of a class that extends `Error` shows the class name before the message. Catch it with `or_else`, or make sure the condition that leads to `fail` cannot happen.
errors.example:
func withdraw(number balance, number amount) do:
    if amount > balance do:
        fail "not enough money"
    end
    return balance - amount
end
print(withdraw(10, 50))
errors.report:
[E7-001] Program Error at line 3, column 9
  |
3 |         fail "not enough money"
  |         ^^^^ not enough money

  in withdraw, called from:
    line 7: print(withdraw(10, 50))

errors.name: InternalError
errors.meaning: A bug in the engine: please report it.
errors.detail: **`E9-001`** is a bug in the engine. If you meet it, please [report it](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs) with the smallest program that shows it.

limits.name: Source size
limits.description: The largest program, module file or shell entry. Each file is measured on its own.

limits.name: Nesting depth
limits.description: How deeply code may nest: blocks, parentheses, brackets, call arguments. The parser recurses on the native stack, so this also stops hostile input from exhausting it. It is checked against the stack that is really available as well, so on a very small stack it can trigger sooner.

limits.name: Expression length
limits.description: How tall one expression's tree may be: the operators, indexes and slices in one chain such as `a + b + c`, or the levels of nested expressions. Long chains are evaluated and freed without recursion, so this does not depend on the stack; it bounds the memory and time one expression can cost.

limits.name: Call depth
limits.description: How many function calls may be active at once. A call takes a frame of the bytecode machine and no native stack, so this is the limit that ends runaway recursion, whatever the function's body looks like.

limits.name: Stack budget ceiling
limits.description: The most native stack the engine may use, however much the host offers or an embedder asks for.

limits.name: Default stack budget
limits.description: The engine's native stack budget when the real stack size cannot be determined (8 MiB in WebAssembly). When it can, the budget is derived from it instead: everything but a safety margin, up to the ceiling above, and never more than the thread really has even if a larger budget is configured. A program's own calls do not draw on it. What does is work that nests inside the engine: the compiler following nested blocks, an object's `to_str` run while a value is shown, a field's default value that makes another object, a module that loads a module.

limits.name: String size
limits.description: The longest string a program can build.

limits.name: List and map size
limits.description: The most elements one list or map can hold.

limits.name: Value nesting in output
limits.description: How deeply nested lists and maps are written out when printed or converted to text; anything deeper is shown as `[...]` or `{...}`.

limits.name: JSON nesting
limits.description: How deeply nested the text `from_json` reads, or the value `to_json` writes, may be.

limits.name: Tasks
limits.description: How many tasks may exist at once that have not finished: those that have not started yet, and those that wait.

limits.name: Waiting tasks
limits.description: How many tasks may be waiting at once (for another task, for `time_sleep`, for a network answer). A task that has started keeps its variables until it finishes, which one that has not started does not.

limits.name: PBKDF2 iterations
limits.description: The most rounds `hash_pbkdf2_sha256` may be asked for. Ten million take a few seconds, and the time limit is looked at when the call returns.

limits.name: PBKDF2 key length
limits.description: The longest key, in bytes, `hash_pbkdf2_sha256` may be asked to derive.

limits.name: Sleep
limits.description: The longest `time_sleep` may be asked to wait, in seconds (1000 days).

limits.name: Class inheritance depth
limits.description: How many parent classes one class may have in a chain (`extends` of `extends` of ...).

limits.name: Members per class
limits.description: The most fields and methods one class can have, counting the ones it inherits. It also bounds the size of every object of that class.

limits.name: Classes
limits.description: The most classes a program can declare, modules included. The built-in `Error` class does not count.

limits.name: Module nesting
limits.description: How many levels of modules may import other modules.

limits.name: HTTP connect timeout (ms)
limits.description: How long `DLC:network` waits to connect.

limits.name: HTTP total timeout (ms)
limits.description: How long one `DLC:network` request may take in all.

limits.name: HTTP response size
limits.description: The largest response `DLC:network` accepts.

limits.name: HTTP redirects
limits.description: How many redirects `DLC:network` follows.

limits.name: Pattern group nesting
limits.description: How deeply the groups of one pattern may nest.

limits.name: Pattern size
limits.description: The longest pattern.

limits.name: Pattern repeat count
limits.description: The largest count in a repeat such as `[num]100000`.
